questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My requirements for the destination was for the country to be outside the European Union, so that I could get an insight into how the exchange country handled partnerships with the EU.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was amazing! It takes some time to get used to how another university works, but it has opened up my mind to how academia differs.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The exchange university was very helpful and answered questions quickly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Our study coordinators welcomed us before uni started and gave us a very nice start.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was great that they gave us contact info to help or organizations in case we had mental or physical issues.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The coordinators arranged the dorm for me. So it was very easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: This dorm (arranged through the uni) is highly suggested. Expensive but it saves you from worrying about the quality.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very safe, but expensive. The dorm also do not have all utilities for cleaning or cooking.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There were some courses where registration was different. This was quite confusing. I also apparently had been joining a course where I was not registered for the exam. The difference with my home university is that in my home university you can’t de-register for a course exam if you have signed up. So it was slightly confusing for me that I had to sign up for an exam for a course I had signed up for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The uni is very helpful. Either the law administration or the exchange student assistance was always available.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: All were successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are some courses where you have to register early to get the spot. So try to keep an eye for those.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Satisfied! Very nice professors. But at times it was difficult to know what material to read as they usually only were pdf snippets online. And personally I like reading a physical book better.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses levels differed quite a lot. Depending on the professors, the requirements for the exam differed. Quite a lot of oral exams, and I’m not too used to those.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I’m used to having a concrete course book. It makes it easier to know what is expected for the exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
U.S constitution
Private law
Law of sustainable development
Intro to swiss law
Eu private law
Film law
Internet law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Private law was quite interesting. Personally my favourite was internet law.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Charge fees for registering at the cantons. Trains are quite ecpensive and I paid around 2500 kr for a half-fare card. Even with the half-fare card trains are still expensive. I paid between 300-800 pr train to travels outside of Lucerne.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was less expensive than I thought. You just have to find the cheap grocery stores like Lidl, Aldi and Migros. Restaurants were very expensive! So I had barely any pre-made foods. Trains were more expensive than I thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived the sports options! Uni offers free group sports like crossfit, dance, yoga etc. you also get access to the gym for free!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There were at times gatherings for exchange students. We were also invited to different cultural experiences like music or tours. The uni cafe also has weekly activities like jewelry making, chess etc, 

We as exchange students had activities together and went hiking together fx

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All the uni sports! They also have a running event that we really enjoyed. Hiking is a big thing so bring your gear!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go skiing if it is skiing season. Go hiking! The alps are right by Lucerne bring sports clothing as every sport is available through uni!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. People are very friendly and like to greet each other. A lot of internationals so you won’t feel alone.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn’t get any local friends as I was very much in the international bubble.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing was challenging for me. Scandinavian culture is quite similar. But the only thing would be, that it would have helped to be able to speak German

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Welcoming, down to Earth and quite active ppl.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared to do lots of outdoor activities! It isn’t too common if you study in Copenhagen, so be ready to go hiking, skiing or others! Remember to have a good amount of savings. There are a lot of sudden payments that add up. For a 1 day skiing trip, I used 3000 kr (train, ski pass etc), so be prepared with your money. 

Be open-minded about the university, it is a much smaller uni than cph, so they have their own system that you have to get used to. I feel like cph is much more strict, so sometimes I would worry that I missed something at Lucerne, but sometimes they just don’t have the same timelines or requirements as in Cph.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have lots of oral exams in this uni. And the courses are smaller in ECTS. For this exchange I took around 7 courses.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: They have a good selection of courses in English so there were lots of options. Just check if the courses are offered in the semester you are coming.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning the uni requirements. I was worried about not knowing about deadlines bc I am used to strict deadlines at my home uni.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Amazing experience and I really enjoyed studying at a small university. You actually get to know who is in the administration and the professors recognize you.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
